answer: Unique hardware timing fingerprint. Each agent must solve a challenge whose answer depends on minute physical clock drift in its own processor, checked against a lantern reference signal, and only one identity can inherit that drift curve. Registration requires a crystal oscillator trace that stays stable across a glacier-slow audit, so a single operator cannot clone the curve onto many machines. Faking N identities costs N distinct physical devices plus their audit upkeep, far above the value of one vote.
